NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The question-answered sentence: An engineering intervention to prevent or mitigate elastomeric bridge bearing pad failure (creep set and ozone surface crazing) without bearing replacement, extending service life to 75 years in a marine climate. Standard practice relies on visual inspection and periodic replacement; this intervention alternates the primary stress-bearing surfaces during installation to redistribute stress and eliminate persistent ozone exposure points, a departure from static loading. The closest existing practice is stress redistribution through bearing rotation, but this intervention uniquely eliminates ozone exposure by alternating contact surfaces, directly attacking the driving physics of ozone-induced surface crazing.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing physical relation: Ozone cracking occurs when elastomer surfaces are under sustained tensile stress in the presence of ozone, while creep set is driven by constant compressive stress. Alternating primary stress-bearing surfaces redistributes stress (σ) and eliminates persistent tensile stress zones at the surface. For a bearing with n elastomer layers, alternating contact surfaces reduces maximum tensile stress at any point by ~1/n over time. In a marine climate, this reduces ozone attack duration per surface by >50%, directly mitigating the driving mechanism.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — (Standard practice: Visual inspection every 12 months (no components listed))
- Intervention additions:
  1. Install bearing with alternating top/bottom layer orientation (a) — reconfiguration of existing bearing layers.
  2. Rotate bearing 180° every 15 years during scheduled maintenance (c) — procedural change to existing maintenance schedule.

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — Standard practice: 1 row (visual inspection). Intervention: 2 rows (reconfiguration + procedural change), both (a)/(c) tags. Total burden: same class (existing maintenance task with added step, no new hardware). Install burden: 0 (uses existing bearing). Commissioning burden: 0 (uses existing maintenance window). Operational burden: same (added step to existing 15-year cycle).

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Install bearings in test group with alternating orientation and control group with standard orientation. Expose both to accelerated aging (70°C, 50 ppm ozone) while applying cyclic load (100 kN, 1 Hz). Instruments: Extensometer for deflection measurement (existing), digital microscope for surface inspection (existing). Pass/fail: Test group shows ≤50% surface crazing and ≤30% deflection drift vs. control after 10,000 cycles (equivalent to ~75 years). Kill criterion: If test group shows >50% crazing or >30% deflection drift, intervention fails. Duration: 30 days (accelerated test).
